_comment: Accepted response-example gaps. CATS compares a 2xx response to the operation's example, not its schema (Endava/cats#206), so a property the schema declares but the example omits becomes a finding once the server returns it. This file is a ratchet -- it may shrink, never grow, and a new gap fails the build. Down from 611 gaps across 93 operations to 96 across 13 (#659); what is left is not merely unexercised, it is unsatisfiable, in three classes. (1) 90 entries under a oneOf/anyOf union: the checker unions every branch's properties because a response may be any branch, so satisfying it would mean one example cell carrying both node-only properties (position, size, ports) and edge-only ones (source, target, vertices). That document would satisfy CATS and describe nothing real. Covers cells.* on the six diagram operations and diagrams.* on GET /threat_models/{id}. (2) 5 entries whose schema is a free-form object with no declared properties -- deliveries.payload, survey_json, provider_config -- the same class as MinimalDiagramModel.metadata and RollbackResponse.restored_entity. (3) 1 entry where the schema is simply wrong rather than unexercised: subscriptions.secret is declared on the read schema but webhook_handlers.go passes includeSecret=false on both GET paths, and the property's own description says it is not returned. Completing that example would document a secret the endpoint never emits, which is worse than the gap.
